  # classification under the lock, and only there rewrites the file.
  [ "${LOCK_HELD:-0}" = 1 ] || return 0
  [ "$(readlink "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$OWNER" ] || return 1
  repair_next="$STATE_DIR/identity.repair.$$"
  cp -p "$STATE_DIR/identity" "$STATE_DIR/identity.unverified" &&
    printf '%s
' "$repair_identity" >"$repair_next" && mv -f "$repair_next" "$STATE_DIR/identity" ||
    { rm -f "$repair_next"; return 1; }
  verify_owned_identity "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT"
}
check_live_protocol() {
  LIVE_STATUS=none; LIVE_PID=0; LIVE_PORT=0; LIVE_VERSION=unknown
  LIVE_COMPATIBLE=0; LIVE_OWNED=0; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=0; REPLACEMENT_REASON=incompatible; comparison=
  LIVE_DRAIN=0; LIVE_INSTANCE_ID=; DEFER_NO_DRAIN=0
  if live="$(live_fact "$CHECK_RUNNER" "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" "$PORT_FILE" "$PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    set -f; set -- $live
    if ! valid_live_tokens "$@"; then printf 'Malformed live protocol output.
' >&2; exit 1; fi
    LIVE_STATUS="$1"; LIVE_VERSION="$2"; LIVE_PID="$5"; LIVE_PORT="$6"
    if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ] && valid_positive "$LIVE_PID" &&
       fact_file_is "$MANAGED_FILE" managed && fact_file_is "$PID_FILE" "$LIVE_PID" &&
       fact_file_is "$PORT_FILE" "$LIVE_PORT"; then LIVE_OWNED=1; fi
    if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ]; then read_live_compat "$2" "$3" "$4"; fi
    if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 0 ] && adopt_managed_orphan; then LIVE_OWNED=1; fi
  else
    if [ -e "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" ] || [ -e "$PORT_FILE" ] || [ -e "$PID_FILE" ]; then LIVE_STATUS=unknown; fi
  fi
  DRAIN_UNCERTAIN=0
  if [ -e "$STATE_DIR/draining" ] || [ -L "$STATE_DIR/draining" ]; then
    fact_slurp "$STATE_DIR/draining" || FACT_TEXT=; draining_instance="$FACT_TEXT"
    if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = none ] ||
       { [ -n "$draining_instance" ] && [ -n "$LIVE_INSTANCE_ID" ] && [ "$draining_instance" != "$LIVE_INSTANCE_ID" ]; }; then
      # Only an owner can retire a fence after the live helper proves its start is gone.
      if [ "$LOCK_HELD" = 1 ] && [ "$(readlink "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$OWNER" ]; then
        rm -f "$STATE_DIR/draining"
      fi
    else DRAIN_UNCERTAIN=1; fi
  fi
  if [ "$ALLOW_LEGACY_ADOPTION" = 1 ] &&
     { [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = unknown ] || { [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ ! -e "$STATE_DIR/identity" ] && [ ! -L "$STATE_DIR/identity" ]; }; }; then
    legacy_verified=1
    if [ "$LEGACY_COMMITTED" = 1 ]; then
      verify_owned_identity "$LEGACY_PID" "$LEGACY_PORT" || ownership_unverified
    elif ! verify_legacy_identity; then legacy_verified=0; LIVE_STATUS=unknown; fi
    if [ "$legacy_verified" = 1 ] && [ "$LEGACY_PENDING" = 1 ]; then
      LIVE_STATUS=live; LIVE_PID="$LEGACY_PID"; LIVE_PORT="$LEGACY_PORT"; LIVE_VERSION="$LEGACY_VERSION"
      LIVE_OWNED=1; REPLACEMENT_REASON=legacy; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$LEGACY_PENDING" != 1 ] &&
     [ ! -e "$STATE_DIR/identity" ] && [ ! -L "$STATE_DIR/identity" ]; then LIVE_STATUS=unknown; fi
  if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = unknown ]; then
    fact_slurp "$PID_FILE" || FACT_TEXT=; recorded_pid="$FACT_TEXT"
    fact_slurp "$PORT_FILE" || FACT_TEXT=; recorded_port="$FACT_TEXT"
    valid_positive "$recorded_pid" || recorded_pid=unknown
    valid_positive "$recorded_port" || recorded_port=unknown
    stop_pid="$recorded_pid"
    [ "$stop_pid" != unknown ] || stop_pid='<pid>'
    printf 'Cannot verify live GOAT PID=%s port=%s: descriptor unavailable or persisted identity disagrees; it may predate GOAT SSH runtime protocol metadata. It was left running, and the runner and ownership files were preserved. If this is your earlier GOAT server, stop it on the remote host (kill %s) and reconnect.\n' "$recorded_pid" "$recorded_port" "$stop_pid" >&2; exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LEGACY_PENDING" != 1 ]; then
    verify_owned_identity "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" || repair_owned_identity || ownership_unverified
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ] && [ -n "$REQUESTED_VERSION" ]; then
    if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$SELECTED_VERSION" ] && [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 0 ]; then
      # A retained compatible selection only reuses its proven live version;
      # older compatible helpers need not implement the new replacement comparator.
      comparison=selected
    else
      # Commit times order builds whose versions cannot (dev shas, dev against nightly).
      set --
      if live_commit="$(build_commit_time "$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$LIVE_VERSION/goat")" &&
         requested_commit="$(build_commit_time "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin")"; then
        set -- --live-commit-time "$live_commit" --requested-commit-time "$requested_commit"
      fi
      comparison="$("$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" __ssh-helper compare-version "$@" "$LIVE_VERSION" "$REQUESTED_VERSION" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    case "$comparison" in
      selected) ;;
      newer)
        if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" != 1 ]; then
          printf 'Remote runtime is newer than this app; update the app.
' >&2; exit 1
        fi
        NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=0 ;;
      unknown)
        # No proven order: never replace, so a possibly newer server is never downgraded.
        if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" != 1 ]; then
          printf 'Remote runtime GOAT %s cannot be ordered against this app (GOAT %s); it was left running. Stop it on the remote host when its work is done, then reconnect.
' "$LIVE_VERSION" "$REQUESTED_VERSION" >&2; exit 1
        fi
        NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=0
        # Except a server that cannot issue the sessions this app needs: keeping it would leave
        # the host unusable for those tasks, so an idle refresh replaces it with this build.
        if [ "$REFRESH_IF_IDLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" != legacy ] &&
           lacks_memory_scopes "$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$LIVE_VERSION/goat"; then
          REPLACEMENT_REASON=capability; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
        fi ;;
      older)
        if [ "$REFRESH_IF_IDLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" != legacy ]; then
          REPLACEMENT_REASON=older; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
        fi ;;
      equal) ;;
      *)
        # Exact-version old helpers may lack comparison; no ordering decision is needed.
        if [ "$LIVE_VERSION" != "$REQUESTED_VERSION" ]; then
          printf 'Cannot verify remote version ordering; process was preserved.
' >&2; exit 1
        fi ;;
    esac
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" != 1 ]; then
    if [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ]; then NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
    else printf 'Live GOAT PID=%s port=%s is incompatible; it was left running. Upgrade with the owning client or reconnect.
' "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" >&2; exit 1; fi
  fi
  if [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" != 1 ]; then
    printf 'Secondary preparation cannot replace a live runtime.
' >&2; exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_DRAIN" != 1 ]; then
    if [ "$REFRESH_IF_IDLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] &&
       { [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" = older ] || [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" = capability ]; }; then
      DEFER_NO_DRAIN=1
    elif [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" = legacy ]; then
      printf 'Live GOAT PID=%s port=%s was started by an older app that cannot hand over ownership without draining; it was left running. Stop it on the remote host when its work is done, then reconnect.
' "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" >&2; exit 1
    else
      printf 'Live GOAT PID=%s port=%s is incompatible; it was left running because it cannot drain for a replacement and this app cannot attach to it. Stop it on the remote host when its work is done, then reconnect.
' "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" >&2; exit 1
    fi
  fi
}
read_live_compat() {
  # The pinned helper applies the one protocol-range comparator. A helper that
  # predates it, or a server without integers, falls back to exact fields.
  compat_version="$1"; compat_ssh="$2"; compat_orchestration="$3"
  if compat_tokens="$(compat_fact "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$LIVE_PORT" "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" "$PORT_FILE" "$PID_FILE" "$LIVE_PID" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    set -f; set -- $compat_tokens
    if [ "$#" = 3 ]; then
      case "$1" in
        compatible) LIVE_COMPATIBLE=1 ;;
        unknown) if compatible_fields "$compat_version" "$compat_ssh" "$compat_orchestration"; then LIVE_COMPATIBLE=1; fi ;;
      esac
      case "$3" in
        -|''|*[!A-Za-z0-9-]*) ;;
        *) if [ "$2" = 1 ]; then LIVE_DRAIN=1; LIVE_INSTANCE_ID="$3"; fi ;;
      esac
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if compatible_fields "$compat_version" "$compat_ssh" "$compat_orchestration"; then LIVE_COMPATIBLE=1; fi
}
recheck_selected_before_use() {
  check_retained_runner
  # Never let a vanished ready selection become a network install.
  if [ "$REQUIRE_INSTALLED" = 1 ] && [ -n "$SELECTED_VERSION" ]; then
    selected_dir="$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$SELECTED_VERSION"
    if [ ! -x "$selected_dir/goat" ] || ! fact_file_is "$selected_dir/.install-complete" "$SELECTED_VERSION"; then
      printf 'Selected GOAT runtime disappeared before use.\n' >&2; exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$RUNNER_PUBLISHED" = 1 ]; then
    if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$RUNNER_FILE"; then
      printf 'Published selected runner changed before use.\n' >&2; exit 1
    fi
    CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_FILE"
  else
    if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$RUNNER_NEXT"; then
      printf 'Candidate runner changed before use.\n' >&2; exit 1
    fi
    CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_NEXT"
  fi
  check_candidate_protocol
  check_live_protocol
  CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
}

check_candidate_protocol
check_live_protocol
if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$RUNNER_NEXT"; then
  printf 'Candidate runner changed during validation; reconnect.
' >&2; exit 1
fi
publish_selected_runner() {
  [ "$(readlink "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$OWNER" ] || {
    printf 'Replacement lock ownership changed; runner was preserved.\n' >&2; exit 1;
  }
  check_retained_runner
if [ -f "$RUNNER_FILE" ] && cmp -s "$RUNNER_NEXT" "$RUNNER_FILE"; then
  rm -f "$RUNNER_NEXT"
else
  mv "$RUNNER_NEXT" "$RUNNER_FILE"
  RUNNER_CHANGED=1
fi
  sync_runner_alias || :
  RUNNER_PUBLISHED=1
}
pending_attachment_safe() {
  [ "$DRAIN_UNCERTAIN" = 0 ] || return 1
  # A replacement needs the mutex; lock-only contention can reuse a proven live server.
  { [ "$LOCK_HELD" = 1 ] && [ "$(readlink "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$OWNER" ]; } ||
    { [ "$reason" = contended ] && [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 0 ]; }
}
emit_pending_only() {
  printf '{"status":"pending","pending":{%s}}
' "$pending_fields"
  exit 0
}
emit_pending() {
  reason="$1"; pending_detail="${2:-}"
  [ -n "$pending_detail" ] || pending_detail="$LOCK_DETAIL"
  pending_fields="$(printf '"reason":"%s","replacement":"%s","requestedVersion":"%s","liveVersion":"%s"' "$reason" "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" "$REQUESTED_VERSION" "$LIVE_VERSION")"
  case "$pending_detail" in
    recovery-stale) pending_fields="$pending_fields,"'"detail":"recovery-stale"' ;;
    drain-unavailable) pending_fields="$pending_fields,"'"refreshCause":"drain_unavailable"' ;;
  esac
  # Reuse is independently proven using the retained runner, never the incompatible candidate.
  pending_attachment_safe || emit_pending_only
  # A server that did not answer its activity probe may not answer the app either; its HTTP
  # root alone does not prove it ready. Only a server without drain support was never asked.
  [ "$reason" != unknown ] || [ "$pending_detail" = drain-unavailable ] || emit_pending_only
  if [ "$reason" = contended ] && [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 0 ] && [ ! -f "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" ]; then
    capture_running_runner || emit_pending_only
  fi

  if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ -f "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" ] &&
     [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" = "$EXPECTED_LIVE_RUNNER_SHA256" ] &&
     [ "$("$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" --version 2>/dev/null || true)" = "goat v$LIVE_VERSION" ]; then
    retained_own="$("$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" __ssh-helper protocol --shell 2>/dev/null || true)"
    set -f; set -- $retained_own
    if valid_own_tokens "$@" && compatible_fields "$1" "$2" "$3" && [ "$1" = "$LIVE_VERSION" ] &&
       "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" __ssh-helper wait-ready "$LIVE_PORT" "2000" "1000" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
      pending_pid="$LIVE_PID"; pending_port="$LIVE_PORT"; pending_version="$LIVE_VERSION"
      check_retained_runner
      check_live_protocol
      pending_attachment_safe || emit_pending_only
      if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_PID" = "$pending_pid" ] && [ "$LIVE_PORT" = "$pending_port" ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$pending_version" ] &&
         { [ "$pending_detail" != drain-unavailable ] || { [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && verify_owned_identity "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT"; }; }; then
        pending_kind=external; [ "$LIVE_OWNED" != 1 ] || pending_kind=managed
        # Lock contention does not imply a replacement; compatible attach-only servers stay ready.
        pending_suffix=
        if [ "$reason" != contended ] || [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" != 0 ]; then
          pending_suffix="$(printf ',"pending":{%s}' "$pending_fields")"
        fi
        printf '{"status":"ready","remotePort":%s,"serverKind":"%s","selectedVersion":"%s"%s}
' "$LIVE_PORT" "$pending_kind" "$LIVE_VERSION" "$pending_suffix"
        exit 0
      fi
    fi
  fi
  emit_pending_only
}
if [ "$OWNING_LAUNCH" = 1 ]; then
  acquire_replacement_lock || { wait_for_replacement_lock && acquire_replacement_lock || emit_pending contended; }
  # Classification and ordering must be fresh under the host-wide mutex.
  CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
  check_live_protocol
  RECONCILING_DRAIN=0
  if [ "$DRAIN_UNCERTAIN" = 1 ]; then
    [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_DRAIN" = 1 ] && [ -n "$LIVE_INSTANCE_ID" ] || emit_pending unknown
    # Retry the authenticated request: the server joins an active drain, confirms its
    # cancellation, or exits for the supervisor. HTTP readiness alone proves none of these.
    RECONCILING_DRAIN=1; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$SELECTED_VERSION" ] &&
     [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$REQUESTED_VERSION" ] && [ -n "$REFRESH_LIVE_VERSION" ] &&
     [ "$REFRESH_LIVE_VERSION" != "$LIVE_VERSION" ]; then
    # Another owner completed this exact refresh while we waited; the old runner pin is obsolete.
    EXPECTED_LIVE_RUNNER_SHA256="$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" || ownership_unverified
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$comparison" = newer ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" != "$SELECTED_VERSION" ]; then
    # Another client may have completed a newer installation since preparation.
    # Pin its independently verified retained runner rather than publish our older candidate.
    selected_dir="$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$LIVE_VERSION"
    [ -x "$selected_dir/goat" ] && [ "$(cat "$selected_dir/.install-complete" 2>/dev/null)" = "$LIVE_VERSION" ] || ownership_unverified
    fresh_sha="$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" || ownership_unverified
    cp "$RUNNER_FILE" "$RUNNER_NEXT"
    [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_NEXT")" = "$fresh_sha" ] && [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" = "$fresh_sha" ] || ownership_unverified
    [ "$("$RUNNER_NEXT" --version 2>/dev/null || true)" = "goat v$LIVE_VERSION" ] || ownership_unverified
    pin_runner "$RUNNER_NEXT"
    SELECTED_VERSION="$LIVE_VERSION"; REQUIRE_INSTALLED=1
    EXPECTED_LIVE_RUNNER_SHA256="$fresh_sha"
    [ "$PRESERVE_SELECTED_RUNNER" = 0 ] || EXPECTED_RETAINED_SHA256="$fresh_sha"
  fi
  check_candidate_protocol
  check_retained_runner
  # Nothing since the check under the lock re-pins or changes its inputs when it found no server,
  # and the launch asks again before it acts on the answer.
  [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = none ] || check_live_protocol
  [ "$RECONCILING_DRAIN" != 1 ] || NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1

  [ "$DEFER_NO_DRAIN" != 1 ] || emit_pending unknown drain-unavailable
  if [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$RECONCILING_DRAIN" != 1 ] && [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" != incompatible ] && [ "$DRAIN_FORCE" != 1 ]; then
    # An optional refresh waits for idle; launch probes again last, then the server drains.
    activity="$(read_refresh_activity)"
    [ "$activity" = idle ] || emit_pending "$activity"
  fi
else
  # Pairing/MCP reuse is read-only; only initial shared setup may publish.
  if [ -f "$RUNNER_FILE" ] && [ "$LIVE_STATUS" != none ]; then
    if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_NEXT" "$RUNNER_FILE"; then
      secondary_sha="$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" || exit 1
      cp "$RUNNER_FILE" "$RUNNER_NEXT"
      [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_NEXT")" = "$secondary_sha" ] && [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" = "$secondary_sha" ] || exit 1
      pin_runner "$RUNNER_NEXT"
      CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
      check_candidate_protocol
      check_live_protocol
    fi
    RUNNER_PUBLISHED=1
  else
    acquire_replacement_lock || { printf 'Another client is replacing the remote runtime.
' >&2; exit 1; }
    check_live_protocol
    publish_selected_runner
  fi
fi


PAIRING_BASE_DIR="$DEFAULT_SERVER_HOME"
recheck_selected_before_use
"$RUNNER_FILE" auth pairing create --base-dir "$PAIRING_BASE_DIR" --json

node.runner:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
GOAT_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH='/fixture/cli entry.mjs'
# Older clients inspect these literal declarations without evaluating the runner.
T3_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH='/fixture/cli entry.mjs'
GOAT_ARCHIVE_VERSION=''
T3_ARCHIVE_VERSION=''
# End of the declarations GOAT reads without running this runner.
goat_runtime_fs() (
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    MINGW* | MSYS* | CYGWIN*) ;;
    *) "$@"; exit $? ;;
  esac
  # mv nests a stage in an existing directory; GNU -T renames onto an empty one, refuses the rest.
  if [ "$1" = mv ]; then set -- mv -T "$2" "$3"; fi
  for delay in 0 1 2 4 8 10 10 10; do
    [ "$delay" = 0 ] || sleep "$delay"
    if [ "$2" = -T ] && { [ -e "$4" ] || [ -L "$4" ]; }; then
      printf 'Cannot publish %s: %s already exists.\n' "$3" "$4" >&2; exit 1
    fi
    if output="$(LC_ALL=C "$@" 2>&1)"; then
      [ -z "$output" ] || printf '%s\n' "$output"
      exit 0
    else
      status=$?
    fi
    case "$output" in
      *'Permission denied'* | *'Device or resource busy'* | *'Access is denied'*) ;;
      *) printf '%s\n' "$output" >&2; exit "$status" ;;
    esac
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$output" >&2
  printf '%s\n' 'An antivirus/real-time scan may be locking the new goat.exe. Consider excluding %USERPROFILE%\.goat\runtime, then retry.' >&2
  exit "$status"
)
goat_runtime_publish() {
  # Another installer may have completed this version during extraction on Windows; keep it.
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    MINGW* | MSYS* | CYGWIN*)
      if [ -x "$2/goat" ] && [ "$(cat "$2/.install-complete" 2>/dev/null)" = "$3" ]; then
        rm -rf "$1" 2>/dev/null || :; return 0
      fi ;;
  esac
  goat_runtime_fs rm -rf "$2"
  goat_runtime_fs mv "$1" "$2"
}
prepend_path_if_dir() {
  if [ -d "$1" ]; then
    case ":$PATH:" in
      *":$1:"*) ;;
      *) PATH="$1:$PATH" ;;
    esac
  fi
}

remote_node_satisfies_engine() {
  GOAT_NODE_ENGINE_RANGE='^22.16 || ^23.11 || >=24.10'
  if [ -z "$GOAT_NODE_ENGINE_RANGE" ]; then
    return 0
  fi
  node - "$GOAT_NODE_ENGINE_RANGE" <<'NODE'
function satisfiesSemverRange(rawVersion, range) {
  const normalizedVersion = String(rawVersion).trim().replace(/^v/, "");
  const versionMatch = normalizedVersion.match(
    /^(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?(?:\.(\d+))?(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$/,
  );
  if (!versionMatch) {
    return false;
  }

  const version = {
    major: Number(versionMatch[1]),
    minor: Number(versionMatch[2] || 0),
    patch: Number(versionMatch[3] || 0),
  };

  return range.split("||").some((group) => {
    const comparators = group.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
    if (comparators.length === 0) {
      return false;
    }
    return comparators.every((comparator) => {
      const match = comparator.trim().match(/^(\^|>=|>|<=|<|=)?\s*v?(\d+(?:\.\d+){0,2})$/);
      if (!match) {
        return false;
      }
      const targetVersion = match[2];
      if (targetVersion === undefined) {
        return false;
      }
      const targetMatch = targetVersion.match(/^(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?(?:\.(\d+))?$/);
      if (!targetMatch) {
        return false;
      }
      const target = {
        major: Number(targetMatch[1]),
        minor: Number(targetMatch[2] || 0),
        patch: Number(targetMatch[3] || 0),
      };
      const compared =
        version.major !== target.major
          ? version.major > target.major
            ? 1
            : -1
          : version.minor !== target.minor
            ? version.minor > target.minor
              ? 1
              : -1
            : version.patch !== target.patch
              ? version.patch > target.patch
                ? 1
                : -1
              : 0;
      const operator = match[1] || "=";
      switch (operator) {
        case "^":
          if (compared < 0) {
            return false;
          }
          if (target.major > 0) {
            return version.major === target.major;
          }
          if (target.minor > 0) {
            return version.major === 0 && version.minor === target.minor;
          }
          return version.major === 0 && version.minor === 0 && version.patch === target.patch;
        case ">=":
          return compared >= 0;
        case ">":
          return compared > 0;
        case "<=":
          return compared <= 0;
        case "<":
          return compared < 0;
        case "=":
          return compared === 0;
        default:
          return false;
      }
    });
  });
}
var range = process.argv[2] || "";
var rawVersion =
  process.versions && process.versions.node ? process.versions.node : process.version;
if (!satisfiesSemverRange(rawVersion, range)) {
  process.stderr.write(
    "Remote node " + rawVersion + " does not satisfy required range " + range + ".\n",
  );
  process.exit(1);
}
NODE
}

ensure_remote_node_path() {
  if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && remote_node_satisfies_engine >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi

  prepend_path_if_dir "$HOME/.local/bin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "$HOME/bin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "/opt/homebrew/bin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "/usr/local/bin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "/usr/bin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "/bin"
  # lsof lives in sbin on macOS. A login PATH that already has node returns
  # before these lines, so the launch script also prepends them unconditionally.
  prepend_path_if_dir "/usr/sbin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "/sbin"

  if [ -z "${VOLTA_HOME:-}" ]; then
    VOLTA_HOME="$HOME/.volta"

    major: Number(versionMatch[1]),
    minor: Number(versionMatch[2] || 0),
    patch: Number(versionMatch[3] || 0),

      return false;

      const match = comparator.trim().match(/^(\^|>=|>|<=|<|=)?\s*v?(\d+(?:\.\d+){0,2})$/);

        return false;
      }

        return false;
      }

        return false;
      }

        major: Number(targetMatch[1]),
        minor: Number(targetMatch[2] || 0),
        patch: Number(targetMatch[3] || 0),

        version.major !== target.major
          ? version.major > target.major
            ? 1
            : -1
          : version.minor !== target.minor
            ? version.minor > target.minor
              ? 1
              : -1
            : version.patch !== target.patch
              ? version.patch > target.patch

                : -1

        case "^":

          }

            return version.major === 0 && version.minor === target.minor;
          }

          return compared >= 0;
        case ">":
          return compared > 0;
        case "<=":
          return compared <= 0;

# day before; the whole row, executable path included, is the key. A server GOAT restarts still
# misses: it rewrites the runtime record, whose startedAt and instanceId are in the key.
# Rows are read with shell builtins, as the awk program they replace read them: ps's status is
# ignored, a leading status letter is dropped and fields join with one space. WINPIDs compare as
# numbers, as awk compared them: digits without their leading zeros. Any other numeric spelling
# (5678.0, +5678) or more than 15 digits, beyond which awk's doubles can equate two of them, makes

    [ -z "$2" ] || FACT_START2="$(LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC ps -o lstart= -p "$2" 2>/dev/null)" || FACT_START2=

    fact_pid_number "${4:-}" || ps_odd=1

    [ -z "$ps_b" ] || [ -n "$FACT_START2" ] || [ "$FACT_TEXT" != "$ps_b" ] || FACT_START2="$*"

# Sets FACT_TEXT to $1 as awk compares it with a PID: digits lose their leading zeros, and other

# digits, which a double may not hold exactly.
fact_pid_number() {
  FACT_TEXT="$1"
  case "$1" in
    '') return 0 ;;
    *[!0123456789]*)

      return 0 ;;
  esac

# Sets FACT_TEXT to the digits after the last JSON name $1 (quoted) in $2 that a colon and a

fact_json_uint() {
  FACT_TEXT=; json_rest="$2"
  while :; do
    case "$json_rest" in *"$1"*) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
    json_tail="${json_rest##*"$1"}"; json_rest="${json_rest%"$1"*}"
    while :; do case "$json_tail" in [[:space:]]*) json_tail="${json_tail#?}" ;; *) break ;; esac; done
    case "$json_tail" in :*) json_tail="${json_tail#:}" ;; *) continue ;; esac
    while :; do case "$json_tail" in [[:space:]]*) json_tail="${json_tail#?}" ;; *) break ;; esac; done

# Sets FACT_TEXT to file $1 as tr '\n' ' ' <"$1" prints it: every line ended by a space.

# Compatibility tokens from goat $1 for the server on port $2, keyed like live_fact by $3-$5.

# Key $2 counts when any line declares it, else key $3; quoted values only. Builtins only: an
# MSYS fork costs about 50 ms. The comparison test pins this against the grep and sed reader.
hint_nl='
'
hint_end='# End of the declarations GOAT reads without running this runner.'
# Adds line $1 to the declarations of keys $2/$3 and, with five arguments, $4/$5.
hint_take() {
  case "$1" in "$2="*) hint_named=1 ;; esac
  case "$1" in "$2='"*"'") hint_value="${1#"$2='"}"; hint_want="$hint_want${hint_value%"'"}$hint_nl" ;; esac
  case "$1" in "$3='"*"'") hint_value="${1#"$3='"}"; hint_back="$hint_back${hint_value%"'"}$hint_nl" ;; esac
  if [ "$#" -ge 5 ]; then
    case "$1" in "$4="*) hint_named2=1 ;; esac
    case "$1" in "$4='"*"'") hint_value="${1#"$4='"}"; hint_want2="$hint_want2${hint_value%"'"}$hint_nl" ;; esac

# Sets RUNNER_HINT for key $2 (else $3) and, when $4 is given, RUNNER_HINT2 for key $4 (else $5),
# as $(...) would keep them, from every line of runner $1. bash reads the file in one call and,
# when no line after the end-of-declarations line starts with a key, parses only the lines
# before it, which give the same answer; other shells and files with NUL bytes read each line.
runner_hint_set() {
  RUNNER_HINT=; RUNNER_HINT2=; hint_line=

helper_caps_old='

helper_caps() {

# writes.
frame_direct_call() {

      printf '%s\n' "$?" >"$FACT_MEMO.facts-status"; } | head -c 1 >"$FACT_MEMO.facts-err" 3>&-; } 3>&1 |

# more are missing, and its answers are recorded under the rules of the calls they stand for:

# its second misses; live only as live_fact would keep it, bound to a live key that held across the

# since, the record never named the launched server, or the call failed or printed anything but a
# whole valid frame with a ready answer for REMOTE_PORT or a failure and live and compat answers
# that pass their validators. A wait is a read, so the separate wait then runs, which a ready
# server answers at once. Live and compat are recorded only for the record's own server, REMOTE_PID
# on REMOTE_PORT, when its live key was present before the call and unchanged after it, the runner
# still runs the executable the lookup was for, and both pass the checks live_fact and compat_fact
# record by.
launch_ready_report() {
  LAUNCH_READY=1
  [ -n "$LAUNCH_CAPS_FILE" ] && [ -f "$LAUNCH_CAPS_FILE" ] || return 1
  { IFS= read -r report_caps_key && IFS= read -r report_caps; } <"$LAUNCH_CAPS_FILE" || return 1
  case " $report_caps " in *" wait-ready-report "*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  report_exe="$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$SELECTED_VERSION/goat"
  exec_fact_key "$report_exe" && [ "$FACT_KEY" = "$report_caps_key" ] || return 1
  launch_record_wait || return 1
  report_before=; ! live_fact_key "$RUNNER_FILE" "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" "$PORT_FILE" "$PID_FILE" || report_before="$FACT_KEY"
  launch_bounded $(( ($1 + 999) / 1000 + 10 )) "$RUNNER_FILE" __ssh-helper wait-ready "$REMOTE_PORT" "$1" "1000" \
    --report --runtime-file "$LAUNCH_REPORT_RUNTIME" --port-file "$LAUNCH_REPORT_PORT" --pid-file "$LAUNCH_REPORT_PID" >"$FACT_MEMO.report" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  fact_slurp "$FACT_MEMO.report" || return 1
  frame_parse wait-ready "ready live" "$FACT_TEXT" || return 1
  case "$FRAME_READY" in "ok $REMOTE_PORT") LAUNCH_READY=0 ;; "fail "*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  case "$FRAME_LIVE" in "ok "*) (set -f; set -- ${FRAME_LIVE#ok }; valid_live_tokens "$@") || return 1 ;; esac
  case "$FRAME_COMPAT" in "ok "*) facts_frame_compat_valid "${FRAME_COMPAT#ok }" || return 1 ;; esac
  [ "$LAUNCH_READY" = 0 ] && [ -n "$report_before" ] || return 0
  live_fact_key "$RUNNER_FILE" "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" "$PORT_FILE" "$PID_FILE" && [ "$FACT_KEY" = "$report_before" ] || return 0
  report_name="$FACT_NAME"; report_runner="$fact_live"
  exec_fact_key "$report_exe" && [ "$FACT_KEY" = "$report_caps_key" ] &&
    [ "${report_runner% *}" = "${report_caps_key% *}" ] || return 0
  case "$FRAME_LIVE" in "ok "*) report_live="${FRAME_LIVE#ok }" ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
  case "$FRAME_COMPAT" in "ok "*) report_compat="${FRAME_COMPAT#ok }" ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
  fact_valid live "$report_live" && fact_valid compat "$report_compat" || return 0
  facts_frame_live_ids "$report_live"
  [ "$frame_pid" = "$REMOTE_PID" ] && [ "$frame_port" = "$REMOTE_PORT" ] &&
    fact_bound "$frame_pid" "$frame_port" || return 0
  fact_put "live.$report_name" "$report_before" "$report_live"
  fact_put "compat.$report_name" "$report_before|$frame_port" "$report_compat"
}

# macOS login shells often omit /usr/sbin, which is where lsof lives, and archive
# launches never call ensure_remote_node_path. Resolve lsof without that PATH.
ensure_listener_path() {
  prepend_path_if_dir "/usr/sbin"
  prepend_path_if_dir "/sbin"
  export PATH
}
listener_lsof() {
  if command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v lsof
    return 0
  fi
  for candidate in /usr/sbin/lsof /sbin/lsof; do
    if [ -x "$candidate" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  return 1
}
listener_probe_available() {
  if [ "$GOAT_HOST_WINDOWS" = 1 ]; then return 0; fi
  if [ -d /proc/self/fd ]; then return 0; fi

}
# netstat answers in about 0.15 s where a PowerShell start takes 1.5 s, but its state word is
# localized on some display languages. It proves server $1 owns 127.0.0.1:$2 only after it exited
# 0 within 5 s and its whole output has exactly one row from 127.0.0.1:$2 to 0.0.0.0:0, and it is
# TCP 127.0.0.1:$2 0.0.0.0:0 LISTENING $1. Output that ends mid-line was cut short and proves nothing.
# Bash only. read -d '' takes the file whole and succeeds only at a NUL byte, which netstat never
# prints (a command substitution would drop it).
listener_netstat_owns() {
  if launch_bounded 5 netstat.exe -ano -p TCP </dev/null >"$STATE_DIR/netstat.$$" 2>/dev/null; then
    listener_status=0; else listener_status=1; fi
  listener_netstat=
  if IFS= read -r -d '' listener_netstat 2>/dev/null <"$STATE_DIR/netstat.$$"; then listener_status=1; fi
  rm -f "$STATE_DIR/netstat.$$" || :
  [ "$listener_status" = 0 ] || return 1
  listener_pid="$1"; listener_port="$2"; listener_found=1
  printf -v listener_cr '\r'; printf -v IFS ' \t'; set -f
  while :; do
    case "$listener_netstat" in *"
"*) ;; *) [ -z "$listener_netstat" ] || return 1; break ;; esac
    listener_line="${listener_netstat%%"
"*}"
    listener_netstat="${listener_netstat#*"
"}"
    set -- ${listener_line%"$listener_cr"}
    [ "$#" -ge 3 ] && [ "$1" = TCP ] && [ "$2" = "127.0.0.1:$listener_port" ] && [ "$3" = 0.0.0.0:0 ] || continue
    [ "$#" = 5 ] && [ "$4" = LISTENING ] && [ "$5" = "$listener_pid" ] || return 1
    case "$5" in ''|*[!0123456789]*) return 1 ;; esac
    [ "$listener_found" = 1 ] || return 1

  done

}
server_owns_listener() (
  # Protocol parsing leaves noglob enabled; socket fd discovery needs expansion.
  set +f

    if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && listener_netstat_owns "$1" "$2"; then return 0; fi
    GOAT_PROCESS_ID="$1" GOAT_LISTEN_PORT="$2" launch_bounded 15 powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand '' </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
  elif [ -d /proc/self/fd ]; then
    listen_sockets=' '
    for listen_fd in /proc/"$1"/fd/*; do
      listen_socket="$(readlink "$listen_fd" 2>/dev/null)" || continue
      case "$listen_socket" in socket:*) listen_sockets="$listen_sockets$listen_socket " ;; esac
    done
    listen_address="$(printf '0100007F:%04X' "$2")" || return 1
    awk -v address="$listen_address" -v sockets="$listen_sockets" '
      $2 == address && $4 == "0A" && index(sockets, " socket:[" $10 "] ") { found=1 }
      END { exit !found }

    lsof_bin="$(listener_lsof)" || return 1

)
# Sets launch_now_us to the wall clock in microseconds without a process where it can: bash 5's
# EPOCHREALTIME (its decimal point follows the locale), else SECONDS from one date per script.
LAUNCH_EPOCH_BASE=
launch_now() {
  launch_now_us="${EPOCHREALTIME:-}"
  case "$launch_now_us" in
    *[.,]*)
      launch_now_us="${launch_now_us%[.,]*}${launch_now_us#*[.,]}"
      case "$launch_now_us" in ''|*[!0123456789]*) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac ;;
  esac
  if [ -z "${SECONDS:-}" ]; then launch_now_us=$(( $(date +%s) * 1000000 )); return 0; fi
  [ -n "$LAUNCH_EPOCH_BASE" ] || LAUNCH_EPOCH_BASE=$(( $(date +%s) - SECONDS ))
  launch_now_us=$(( (LAUNCH_EPOCH_BASE + SECONDS) * 1000000 ))
}
# fd 7 is a private FIFO that only carries this shell's job list: bash lists it there and reads it
# back, and waits on it with read -t, so a pass starts no process. Its name is removed once open (the
# launch's EXIT trap removes it too). Any failed step falls back to tr and sleep, as does bash before
# 4, which crashes after a function that ran command exec returns and cannot read -t 0.05.
LAUNCH_FIFO=
launch_fifo_open() {
  LAUNCH_FIFO=0
  [ "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}" -ge 4 ] || return 0
  # A killed script can leave its name behind. Only names of shells kill -0 finds gone are removed:
  # a live script's name stays, and one that loses its name before opening it falls back to sleep.
  case "$-" in *f*) launch_fifo_glob=1; set +f ;; *) launch_fifo_glob= ;; esac
  for launch_fifo_stale in "$STATE_DIR"/launch-tick.*; do
    launch_fifo_pid="${launch_fifo_stale##*.}"
    case "$launch_fifo_pid" in ''|*[!0123456789]*) continue ;; esac
    if [ -p "$launch_fifo_stale" ] && ! kill -0 "$launch_fifo_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      rm -f "$launch_fifo_stale" || :
    fi
  done
  [ -z "$launch_fifo_glob" ] || set -f
  if mkfifo "$STATE_DIR/launch-tick.$$" 2>/dev/null; then
    if { command exec 7<>"$STATE_DIR/launch-tick.$$"; } 2>/dev/null; then LAUNCH_FIFO=1; fi
    rm -f "$STATE_DIR/launch-tick.$$" || :
  fi
}
launch_fifo_close() { LAUNCH_FIFO=0; exec 7<&-; }
# Waits $1 microseconds.
launch_pause() {
  launch_pause_s=$(( $1 % 1000000 + 1000000 )); launch_pause_s="$(( $1 / 1000000 )).${launch_pause_s#1}"
  if [ "$LAUNCH_FIFO" = 1 ]; then
    if read -t "$launch_pause_s" -u 7 launch_pause_line 2>/dev/null; then launch_pause_r=0; else launch_pause_r=$?; fi
    [ "$launch_pause_r" -le 128 ] || return 0
    launch_fifo_close
  fi
  sleep "$launch_pause_s"
}
# True while the single-process job with PID $1 still runs: bash lists a job as running only until
# it reaps it, so no reused PID can match.
listen_running() {
  if [ "$LAUNCH_FIFO" = 1 ]; then
    if jobs -pr >&7 2>/dev/null && echo . >&7 2>/dev/null; then
      listen_found=1
      while IFS= read -r -t 1 -u 7 listen_line; do
        case "$listen_line" in .) return "$listen_found" ;; "$1") listen_found=0 ;; esac
      done
    fi
    launch_fifo_close
  fi
  case " $(jobs -pr 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ') " in *" $1 "*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
# Ends single-process job $2 through its job spec $1, which bash refuses once the job is reaped and
# never sends to a dead process, so no reused PID is hit (bash loops forever on a pipeline job with
# a dead member). TERM, then KILL after up to 2 s of clock-checked waits; waited for only after.
end_job() {
  kill -TERM "$1" 2>/dev/null || :
  launch_now; end_job_until=$((launch_now_us + 2000000))
  while listen_running "$2" && launch_now && [ "$launch_now_us" -lt "$end_job_until" ]; do launch_pause 100000; done
  if listen_running "$2"; then kill -KILL "$1" 2>/dev/null || :; fi
  wait "$2" 2>/dev/null || :
}
# The bounded job: the command replaces this subshell, so the job is that one process.
launch_bounded_job() { MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' exec "$@"; }
# Windows commands can stall, so after the listener wait starts every one the launch runs goes
# through here: command $2... runs for at most $1 s of clock and returns its own status, or 124 once
# it was ended at the bound. It is checked at once and then after 0.05, 0.1 and every 0.25 s. Other
# hosts, and shells other than bash, whose job specs cannot name it safely, run it directly.
launch_bounded() {
  if [ "$GOAT_HOST_WINDOWS" != 1 ] || [ -z "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then shift; "$@"; return; fi
  [ -n "$LAUNCH_FIFO" ] || launch_fifo_open
  launch_now; launch_bound_until=$((launch_now_us + $1 * 1000000)); shift
  launch_bounded_job "$@" <&0 7<&- &
  launch_bound_job=$!
  launch_bound_step=50000
  while listen_running "$launch_bound_job"; do
    launch_now
    if [ "$launch_now_us" -ge "$launch_bound_until" ]; then
      end_job '%?launch_bounded_job' "$launch_bound_job"; return 124
    fi
    launch_bound_left=$((launch_bound_until - launch_now_us))
    [ "$launch_bound_left" -lt "$launch_bound_step" ] || launch_bound_left="$launch_bound_step"
    launch_pause "$launch_bound_left"
    case "$launch_bound_step" in 50000) launch_bound_step=100000 ;; *) launch_bound_step=250000 ;; esac
  done
  wait "$launch_bound_job"
}
# The launch runs under set -u; these start empty, before any check reads them.
LISTEN_GONE=; LAUNCH_TASKLIST_STALLED=
wait_launched_listener() {
  LISTEN_GONE=
  if [ "$GOAT_HOST_WINDOWS" = 1 ]; then
    launch_now; listen_deadline=$(( launch_now_us / 1000000 + (60000 + 999) / 1000 ))
    # Each PowerShell start costs about 1.5 s, so one waits for the server to own its listener,
    # checking it every 0.1 s: exit 0 once it does, 3 once the server is gone, 4 at the deadline.
    # A failed start (any other exit) is started again before the deadline.
    while launch_now && [ "$launch_now_us" -lt "$((listen_deadline * 1000000))" ]; do
      if GOAT_PROCESS_ID="$REMOTE_PID" GOAT_LISTEN_PORT="$REMOTE_PORT" GOAT_WAIT_UNTIL_MS="$listen_deadline"000 \
        launch_bounded $((listen_deadline - launch_now_us / 1000000)) powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand '' </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
      then listen_status=0; else listen_status=$?; fi
      case "$listen_status" in
        0) launch_now; [ "$launch_now_us" -lt "$((listen_deadline * 1000000))" ] && return 0; return 1 ;;
        3) LISTEN_GONE="$REMOTE_PID"; return 2 ;;
        4|124) return 1 ;;
      esac
      launch_pause 100000
    done
    return 1
  fi
  listen_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + (60000 + 999) / 1000 ))
  while server_alive "$REMOTE_PID"; do
    [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$listen_deadline" ] || return 1
    server_owns_listener "$REMOTE_PID" "$REMOTE_PORT" && return 0
    sleep 0.1
  done
  return 2
}
# After the listener wait. Windows: PowerShell's word that the server is gone stands; otherwise
# tasklist runs bounded to 5 s. Gone is only its localized "INFO: no tasks" answer: exit 0 and one
# line that is no CSV row but holds ": ". Anything else counts as alive, and after a timeout later
# checks in this script do not run tasklist again.
launch_server_alive() {
  [ "$GOAT_HOST_WINDOWS" = 1 ] || { server_alive "$1"; return; }
  [ "${LISTEN_GONE:-}" != "$1" ] || return 1
  [ -z "${LAUNCH_TASKLIST_STALLED:-}" ] || return 0
  if launch_bounded 5 tasklist.exe /FI "PID eq $1" /NH /FO CSV </dev/null >"$STATE_DIR/alive.$$" 2>/dev/null; then
    launch_probe=0; else launch_probe=$?; fi
  if [ "$launch_probe" = 124 ]; then LAUNCH_TASKLIST_STALLED=1; rm -f "$STATE_DIR/alive.$$"; return 0; fi
  launch_alive=0
  if [ "$launch_probe" = 0 ] && LC_ALL=C awk '{ sub(/\r$/, "") } $0 != "" { n++; line = $0 }
    END { exit !(n == 1 && substr(line, 1, 1) != "\"" && index(line, ": ") > 0) }' \
    "$STATE_DIR/alive.$$" 2>/dev/null; then launch_alive=1; fi
  rm -f "$STATE_DIR/alive.$$"
  return "$launch_alive"
}
# Stops server $1 after a failed launch: taskkill is bounded to 10 s, then up to about 2 s for the
# exit. A kill that timed out, or a server still seen or not answered for afterwards, is reported
# as not confirmed stopped.
launch_stop_server() {
  launch_stop_unconfirmed=
  if launch_server_alive "$1"; then
    if [ "$GOAT_HOST_WINDOWS" != 1 ]; then server_kill "$1" || :
    elif launch_bounded 10 taskkill.exe /PID "$1" /F >/dev/null 2>&1; then :
    elif [ "$?" = 124 ]; then launch_stop_unconfirmed=1; fi
  fi
  launch_stop_count=0; launch_stop_until=$(( $(date +%s) + 3 ))
  while [ "$launch_stop_count" -lt 20 ] && [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$launch_stop_until" ] &&
    launch_server_alive "$1"; do
    launch_stop_count=$((launch_stop_count + 1))
    sleep 0.1
  done
  if [ -n "$launch_stop_unconfirmed" ] || launch_server_alive "$1"; then
    printf 'GOAT could not confirm that the server (PID %s) stopped; it may still be running on this host.\n' "$1" >&2
  fi
}

forced_ticks_of() {

forced_trusted() {

    ??????????+*|"") return 1 ;;
    ??????????@*) forced_mode="$(LC_ALL=C ls -lde "$1" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1

  elif [ -z "$forced_recorded_start" ]; then forced_unproven="no start time was recorded at its launch"
  elif [ "$forced_recorded_start" != "$FORCE_START" ]; then forced_unproven="the start time recorded at its launch differs"
  elif [ "$forced_recorded_ticks" != "$(forced_ticks_of "$FORCE_PID")" ]; then forced_unproven="the start tick recorded at its launch differs"
  fi
  if [ -n "$forced_unproven" ]; then
    forced_log_refusal "$forced_unproven"
    printf 'GOAT did not stop PID %s on the remote host: it cannot show this is the runtime it started (the start time recorded at its launch and its launch command must both match, and runtimes started before GOAT kept that record have none). Check it on the host and stop it yourself (kill %s), then update again.\n' "$FORCE_PID" "$FORCE_PID" >&2; exit 1
  fi

  forced_root_ticks="$forced_recorded_ticks"
  forced_parent_holds() {
    server_alive "$FORCE_PID" && [ "$(forced_start_of "$FORCE_PID")" = "$FORCE_START" ] &&
      [ "$(forced_ticks_of "$FORCE_PID")" = "$forced_root_ticks" ]
  }
  # Signals $2 only while it is alive, this user's, started at $4 and tick $5, and with $3 still the
  # child of $3, all read just before the signal.
  forced_signal_same() {
    server_alive "$2" && [ "$(server_uid "$2" | tr -d ' ')" = "$(id -u)" ] &&
      [ "$(forced_start_of "$2")" = "$4" ] && [ "$(forced_ticks_of "$2")" = "$5" ] &&
      { [ -z "$3" ] || [ "$(ps -o ppid= -p "$2" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')" = "$3" ]; } &&
      kill "-$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null

  # One process table read binds each descendant to its parent, owner and start time, and the
  # table's own row for the runtime must still be the approved process. Every row needs numeric
  # ids (macOS lists nobody as uid -2) and every descendant a whole start time; anything else
  # refuses before a signal. Ancestry walks stop after as many steps as the table has rows.
  forced_table="$(LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC ps -A -o pid= -o ppid= -o uid= -o lstart= 2>/dev/null)" || forced_refused "its process table could not be read"
  forced_root="$(printf '%s\n' "$forced_table" | awk -v root="$FORCE_PID" '$1 == root { start = $4; for (i = 5; i <= NF; i++) start = start " " $i; print $3 " " start }')"
  [ "$forced_root" = "$(id -u) $FORCE_START" ] || forced_refused "the process table shows another process under its PID"
  forced_records="$(printf '%s\n' "$forced_table" | awk -v root="$FORCE_PID" -v me="$(id -u)" '
    $1 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || $2 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || $3 !~ /^-?[0-9]+$/ { bad = 1 }
    { parent[$1] = $2; owner[$1] = $3; fields[$1] = NF; start = $4; for (i = 5; i <= NF; i++) start = start " " $i; started[$1] = start }
    END { if (bad) exit 1; for (pid in parent) { if (owner[pid] != me) continue; up = parent[pid]; for (depth = 0; depth < NR && up != ""; depth++) { if (up == root) { if (fields[pid] != 8) exit 1; print pid " " parent[pid] " " started[pid]; break } up = parent[up] } } }')" || forced_refused "its process table could not be read"
  # Each descendant's start tick is read once, then bound by reading its start time and parent
  # again; one that changed in between cannot be identified and is never signalled.
  forced_children=
  while read -r forced_child forced_parent forced_child_start; do
    valid_positive "$forced_child" || continue
    forced_child_ticks="$(forced_ticks_of "$forced_child")"
    [ "$(forced_start_of "$forced_child")" = "$forced_child_start" ] &&
      [ "$(ps -o ppid= -p "$forced_child" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')" = "$forced_parent" ] || continue
    forced_children="$forced_children$forced_child $forced_parent $forced_child_ticks $forced_child_start
"
  done <<GOAT_FORCED_RECORDS
$forced_records
GOAT_FORCED_RECORDS
  # The stopped version can be started again only when it answered its protocol, its launch
  # identity was verified and its release is still installed; the supervisor then rolls back to it.
  FORCED_PREVIOUS_VERSION=; FORCED_PREVIOUS_IDENTITY=; FORCED_PREVIOUS_RUNNER="$STATE_DIR/forced-runner.previous"
  rm -f "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_RUNNER"
  if [ -f "$RUNNER_FILE" ]; then cp -p "$RUNNER_FILE" "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_RUNNER" || forced_refused "its runner could not be kept"; fi
  if [ "$forced_identity_verified" = 1 ] && valid_version "${FORCED_LIVE_VERSION:-}" &&
     [ -x "$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$FORCED_LIVE_VERSION/goat" ] &&
     fact_file_is "$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$FORCED_LIVE_VERSION/.install-complete" "$FORCED_LIVE_VERSION" &&
     [ -f "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_RUNNER" ] && fact_slurp "$STATE_DIR/identity"; then
    FORCED_PREVIOUS_IDENTITY="$FACT_TEXT"; FORCED_PREVIOUS_VERSION="$FORCED_LIVE_VERSION"
  fi
  # From publication on, a dropped SSH session must not end this script before the stop either
  # happened, with the detached supervisor taking over the start, or was undone.
  trap '' HUP PIPE
  # The new runner is published before the first signal, so a failed publication stops nothing.
  publish_selected_runner
  FORCED_PUBLISHED=1
  # The detached supervisor takes over the start and any rollback after the stop, so a host that
  # cannot run it keeps its runtime.
  nohup true >/dev/null 2>>"$LOG_FILE" </dev/null && [ -x "$RUNNER_FILE" ] ||
    forced_refused "the detached supervisor that starts the new runtime cannot run"
  printf 'Stopping GOAT PID %s (started %s, port %s) for an approved forced update.\n' "$FORCE_PID" "$FORCE_START" "$FORCE_PORT" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || :
  if ! forced_parent_holds; then forced_refused "it changed before the signal"; fi
  server_owns_listener "$FORCE_PID" "$FORCE_PORT" || forced_refused "it no longer listens on port $FORCE_PORT"
  if ! forced_signal_same TERM "$FORCE_PID" "" "$FORCE_START" "$forced_root_ticks" && server_alive "$FORCE_PID"; then
    forced_refused "it changed before the signal"
  fi
  forced_waited=0
  while server_alive "$FORCE_PID" && [ "$forced_waited" -lt "$DRAIN_GRACE_SECONDS" ]; do
    sleep 1 || forced_wait_failed SIGTERM; forced_waited=$((forced_waited + 1))
  done
  if server_alive "$FORCE_PID"; then
    # A process still running that no longer passes the checks may be the runtime after a bad read,
    # so nothing more is signalled or started and its records stay for a person.
    if ! forced_signal_same KILL "$FORCE_PID" "" "$FORCE_START" "$forced_root_ticks" && server_alive "$FORCE_PID"; then
      forced_refused "it no longer matched the approved runtime before SIGKILL"
    fi
    forced_waited=0
    while server_alive "$FORCE_PID" && [ "$forced_waited" -lt 10 ]; do sleep 1 || forced_wait_failed SIGKILL; forced_waited=$((forced_waited + 1)); done
    if forced_parent_holds; then
      forced_restore_runner
      printf 'GOAT PID %s on the remote host did not exit after SIGKILL; the update stopped. See %s.\n' "$FORCE_PID" "$LOG_FILE" >&2; exit 1
    fi
    # Still running but no longer identifiable, as after a failed read: nothing more is started.
    if server_alive "$FORCE_PID"; then forced_refused "it was still running after SIGKILL and could not be identified"; fi
  fi
  # A shell cannot signal a child by anything firmer than its PID, which it may have given up by
  # then, so children are never signalled. A recorded child still running is named for a person.
  printf '%s' "$forced_children" | while read -r forced_child forced_parent forced_child_ticks forced_child_start; do
    [ -n "$forced_child" ] && server_alive "$forced_child" || continue
    [ "$(forced_start_of "$forced_child")" = "$forced_child_start" ] && [ "$(forced_ticks_of "$forced_child")" = "$forced_child_ticks" ] || continue
    printf 'GOAT did not signal child process %s of the stopped runtime, which still runs: a shell cannot prove the PID still names that child. Check it on the host.\n' "$forced_child" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || :
  done || :
  if [ -f "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" ] && sed -n 's/.*"pid"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$FORCE_PID"; then
    rm -f "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" 2>/dev/null || :
  fi
  # The runtime is gone, so a records cleanup that fails must not end the script before the
  # supervisor takes over; it rewrites these records for whatever it starts.
  rm -f "$PID_FILE" "$PORT_FILE" "$MANAGED_FILE" "$STATE_DIR/identity" "$STATE_DIR/draining" "$STATE_DIR/started" "$STATE_DIR/started.ticks" 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'GOAT stopped PID %s but could not remove its launch records; the supervisor replaces them.\n' "$FORCE_PID" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || :
  printf 'Stopped GOAT PID %s for the approved forced update.\n' "$FORCE_PID" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || :
  FORCE_STOP=0; LIVE_STATUS=none; LIVE_PID=0; LIVE_PORT=0
}
if [ "$FORCE_STOP" = 1 ]; then forced_stop_runtime; FORCED_STOPPED_PID="$FORCE_PID"; fi
# After a forced stop and publication, the detached supervisor starts the new runtime on the same
# port, as a normal replacement does: a dropped SSH session cannot stop it, and when the new version
# does not start it restores the data and, if the stopped version can run again, starts it again.
forced_supervise_start() {
  if [ "$GOAT_ARCHIVE_MODE" = 1 ]; then forced_spawn="$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$SELECTED_VERSION/goat"
  else forced_spawn="$GOAT_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH"; fi
  forced_result="$STATE_DIR/replacement.result.$"
  # A result file that survives this removal is stale, so whatever it says is never reported.
  rm -f "$forced_result" 2>/dev/null || :
  forced_stale=0; [ ! -e "$forced_result" ] || forced_stale=1
  set --
  [ -n "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_VERSION" ] || rm -f "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_RUNNER" 2>/dev/null || :
  if [ -n "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_VERSION" ]; then
    set -- --previous-runner "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_RUNNER" --previous-version "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_VERSION" --previous-identity "$FORCED_PREVIOUS_IDENTITY"
  fi
  nohup "$RUNNER_FILE" __ssh-helper supervise --forced --old-stopped --old-pid "$FORCED_STOPPED_PID" --old-instance-id forced --port "$FORCE_PORT" --base-dir "$DEFAULT_SERVER_HOME" --state-dir "$STATE_DIR" --runner "$RUNNER_FILE" --target-version "$TARGET_VERSION" --identity "$forced_spawn serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port $FORCE_PORT --base-dir $DEFAULT_SERVER_HOME" "$@" --ready-timeout-ms "60000" --log "$LOG_FILE" --result "$forced_result" >/dev/null 2>>"$LOG_FILE" </dev/null &
  wait "$!" || true
  forced_status=absent; forced_new_pid=0; forced_new_version=
  if [ "$forced_stale" = 0 ] && [ -s "$forced_result" ]; then read -r forced_status forced_new_pid forced_new_version <"$forced_result" || true; fi
  rm -f "$forced_result" 2>/dev/null || :
  case "$forced_status" in
    replaced)
      # The supervisor already recorded this runtime, its start time included.
      REMOTE_PID="$forced_new_pid"; REMOTE_PORT="$FORCE_PORT"; REMOTE_MANAGED=managed; REFRESH_DECISION=replaced ;;
    stuck)
      printf 'GOAT %s, started as PID %s on the remote host, did not become ready and did not exit after SIGKILL; it was left running and nothing more was started. Check it on the host. See %s.\n' "$forced_new_version" "$forced_new_pid" "$LOG_FILE" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    rolled-back)
      printf 'GOAT %s did not start on the remote host after the approved forced stop of PID %s; GOAT %s was started again. See %s.\n' "$TARGET_VERSION" "$FORCED_STOPPED_PID" "$forced_new_version" "$LOG_FILE" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    absent)
      printf 'GOAT stopped PID %s on the remote host for the approved forced update, but the detached supervisor left no result, so GOAT cannot tell whether a runtime is running there now. Check the host and %s; if nothing runs, update again (no approval is needed).\n' "$FORCED_STOPPED_PID" "$LOG_FILE" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *)
      printf 'GOAT did not start %s on the remote host: after the approved forced stop of PID %s, the detached supervisor reported a failure and started no earlier runtime again. The reason is in %s. Check the host; if nothing runs, update again (no approval is needed).\n' "$TARGET_VERSION" "$FORCED_STOPPED_PID" "$LOG_FILE" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}
# A confirmed drain that names an approved process goes only to that process: a runtime started in
# its place after the approval was never shown to the person.
forced_drain_allowed() {
  valid_positive "$FORCE_PID" || return 0
  [ "$UPGRADE_PID" = "$FORCE_PID" ] && [ "$UPGRADE_PORT" = "$FORCE_PORT" ] &&
    [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$UPGRADE_START" | awk '{ $1 = $1; print }')" = "$FORCE_START" ] && return 0
  printf 'GOAT did not update the remote runtime: PID %s, the runtime you approved stopping, is no longer the one running there (PID %s is). It was left running. Ask again.\n' "$FORCE_PID" "$UPGRADE_PID" >&2; exit 1
}
if [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ]; then
  UPGRADE_PID="$LIVE_PID"; UPGRADE_PORT="$LIVE_PORT"; UPGRADE_VERSION="$LIVE_VERSION"
  UPGRADE_INSTANCE="$LIVE_INSTANCE_ID"
  if [ "$GOAT_HOST_WINDOWS" = 1 ] &&
     { [ "$GOAT_ARCHIVE_MODE" != 1 ] || [ ! -x "$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$UPGRADE_VERSION/goat" ]; }; then
    # The Windows supervisor restarts installed release executables only.
    printf 'Live GOAT PID=%s port=%s can only be replaced by a GOAT release on this Windows host; it was left running. Stop it when its work is done, then reconnect.\n' "$UPGRADE_PID" "$UPGRADE_PORT" >&2; exit 1
  fi

  check_retained_runner

    verify_legacy_identity || ownership_unverified
  else verify_owned_identity "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" || repair_owned_identity || ownership_unverified; fi
  UPGRADE_START="$(server_start "$UPGRADE_PID")" || ownership_unverified
  [ -n "$UPGRADE_START" ] || ownership_unverified
  forced_drain_allowed
  if [ "$RECONCILING_DRAIN" != 1 ] && [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" != incompatible ] && [ "$DRAIN_FORCE" != 1 ]; then
    # An optional refresh drains only an idle server, so its retries never hold up new turns.
    activity="$(read_refresh_activity)"
    [ "$activity" = idle ] || emit_pending "$activity"
  fi
  if [ "$LEGACY_PENDING" = 1 ] && [ "$LEGACY_COMMITTED" = 0 ]; then
    commit_legacy_identity || ownership_unverified
  fi
  verify_owned_identity "$UPGRADE_PID" "$UPGRADE_PORT" || ownership_unverified
  if [ "$LEGACY_PENDING" = 1 ]; then
    verify_legacy_process "$UPGRADE_PID" "$LEGACY_IDENTITY" || ownership_unverified
  fi
  [ "$(server_start "$UPGRADE_PID")" = "$UPGRADE_START" ] || ownership_unverified
  [ "$(readlink "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$OWNER" ] || ownership_unverified
  PREVIOUS_IDENTITY="$(cat "$STATE_DIR/identity")" || ownership_unverified
  PREVIOUS_RUNNER="$STATE_DIR/run-t3.previous"
  if [ -f "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" ]; then cp -p "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" "$PREVIOUS_RUNNER"

      if forced_target_recorded "$UPGRADE_PID" "$UPGRADE_PORT"; then forced_stop_runtime; DRAIN_FORCED=1; drain_old_stopped=--old-stopped

  if [ "$DRAIN_FORCED" != 1 ]; then

  fi

    SPAWN_IDENTITY="$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$SELECTED_VERSION/goat"
  else
    SPAWN_IDENTITY="$GOAT_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH"
  fi

  rm -f "$SUPERVISE_RESULT" 2>/dev/null || :; supervise_stale=0; [ ! -e "$SUPERVISE_RESULT" ] || supervise_stale=1

runner_hint_set() {

# lines a NUL breaks and x ends, keeps one byte of stderr, and takes the status from a file only it
# writes.
frame_direct_call() {
  : >"$FACT_MEMO.facts-status" || return 1

      printf '%s\n' "$?" >"$FACT_MEMO.facts-status"; } | head -c 1 >"$FACT_MEMO.facts-err" 3>&-; } 3>&1 |
    head -c 4097 | tr '\000' '\n'; printf x)"

    [ ! -s "$FACT_MEMO.facts-err" ] && [ "${#frame_out}" -le 1025 ] || return 1

# protocol --shell and protocol --runtime-file ... --shell do (the same functions in apps/server,
# pinned by its contract test). So one start asks the questions not yet answered, when two or
# more are missing, and its answers are recorded under the rules of the calls they stand for:
# version and own under the pin's exec key, which holds its digest, so a young pin rewritten within
# its second misses; live only as live_fact would keep it, bound to a live key that held across the
# call or, for no server, in this script's memo, which live_fact reads only while all three files

    [ "$stop_pid" != unknown ] || stop_pid='<pid>'
    printf 'Cannot verify live GOAT PID=%s port=%s: descriptor unavailable or persisted identity disagrees; it may predate GOAT SSH runtime protocol metadata. It was left running, and the runner and ownership files were preserved. If this is your earlier GOAT server, stop it on the remote host (kill %s) and reconnect.\n' "$recorded_pid" "$recorded_port" "$stop_pid" >&2; exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LEGACY_PENDING" != 1 ]; then
    verify_owned_identity "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" || repair_owned_identity || ownership_unverified
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ] && [ -n "$REQUESTED_VERSION" ]; then
    if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$SELECTED_VERSION" ] && [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 0 ]; then
      # A retained compatible selection only reuses its proven live version;
      # older compatible helpers need not implement the new replacement comparator.
      comparison=selected
    else
      # Commit times order builds whose versions cannot (dev shas, dev against nightly).
      set --
      if live_commit="$(build_commit_time "$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$LIVE_VERSION/goat")" &&
         requested_commit="$(build_commit_time "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin")"; then
        set -- --live-commit-time "$live_commit" --requested-commit-time "$requested_commit"
      fi
      comparison="$("$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" __ssh-helper compare-version "$@" "$LIVE_VERSION" "$REQUESTED_VERSION" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    case "$comparison" in
      selected) ;;
      newer)
        if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" != 1 ]; then
          printf 'Remote runtime is newer than this app; update the app.
' >&2; exit 1
        fi
        NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=0 ;;
      unknown)
        # No proven order: never replace, so a possibly newer server is never downgraded.
        if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" != 1 ]; then
          printf 'Remote runtime GOAT %s cannot be ordered against this app (GOAT %s); it was left running. Stop it on the remote host when its work is done, then reconnect.
' "$LIVE_VERSION" "$REQUESTED_VERSION" >&2; exit 1
        fi
        NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=0
        # Except a server that cannot issue the sessions this app needs: keeping it would leave
        # the host unusable for those tasks, so an idle refresh replaces it with this build.
        if [ "$REFRESH_IF_IDLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" != legacy ] &&
           lacks_memory_scopes "$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$LIVE_VERSION/goat"; then
          REPLACEMENT_REASON=capability; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
        fi ;;
      older)
        if [ "$REFRESH_IF_IDLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" != legacy ]; then
          REPLACEMENT_REASON=older; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
        fi ;;
      equal) ;;
      *)
        # Exact-version old helpers may lack comparison; no ordering decision is needed.
        if [ "$LIVE_VERSION" != "$REQUESTED_VERSION" ]; then
          printf 'Cannot verify remote version ordering; process was preserved.
' >&2; exit 1
        fi ;;
    esac
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = live ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" != 1 ]; then
    if [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ]; then NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
    else printf 'Live GOAT PID=%s port=%s is incompatible; it was left running. Upgrade with the owning client or reconnect.
' "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" >&2; exit 1; fi
  fi
  if [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" != 1 ]; then
    printf 'Secondary preparation cannot replace a live runtime.
' >&2; exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_DRAIN" != 1 ]; then
    if [ "$REFRESH_IF_IDLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] &&
       { [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" = older ] || [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" = capability ]; }; then
      DEFER_NO_DRAIN=1
    elif [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" = legacy ]; then
      printf 'Live GOAT PID=%s port=%s was started by an older app that cannot hand over ownership without draining; it was left running. Stop it on the remote host when its work is done, then reconnect.
' "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" >&2; exit 1
    else
      printf 'Live GOAT PID=%s port=%s is incompatible; it was left running because it cannot drain for a replacement and this app cannot attach to it. Stop it on the remote host when its work is done, then reconnect.
' "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT" >&2; exit 1
    fi
  fi
}
read_live_compat() {
  # The pinned helper applies the one protocol-range comparator. A helper that
  # predates it, or a server without integers, falls back to exact fields.
  compat_version="$1"; compat_ssh="$2"; compat_orchestration="$3"
  if compat_tokens="$(compat_fact "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$LIVE_PORT" "$DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FILE" "$PORT_FILE" "$PID_FILE" "$LIVE_PID" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    set -f; set -- $compat_tokens
    if [ "$#" = 3 ]; then
      case "$1" in
        compatible) LIVE_COMPATIBLE=1 ;;
        unknown) if compatible_fields "$compat_version" "$compat_ssh" "$compat_orchestration"; then LIVE_COMPATIBLE=1; fi ;;
      esac
      case "$3" in
        -|''|*[!A-Za-z0-9-]*) ;;
        *) if [ "$2" = 1 ]; then LIVE_DRAIN=1; LIVE_INSTANCE_ID="$3"; fi ;;
      esac
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if compatible_fields "$compat_version" "$compat_ssh" "$compat_orchestration"; then LIVE_COMPATIBLE=1; fi
}
recheck_selected_before_use() {
  check_retained_runner
  # Never let a vanished ready selection become a network install.
  if [ "$REQUIRE_INSTALLED" = 1 ] && [ -n "$SELECTED_VERSION" ]; then
    selected_dir="$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$SELECTED_VERSION"
    if [ ! -x "$selected_dir/goat" ] || ! fact_file_is "$selected_dir/.install-complete" "$SELECTED_VERSION"; then
      printf 'Selected GOAT runtime disappeared before use.\n' >&2; exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$RUNNER_PUBLISHED" = 1 ]; then
    if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$RUNNER_FILE"; then
      printf 'Published selected runner changed before use.\n' >&2; exit 1
    fi
    CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_FILE"
  else
    if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$RUNNER_NEXT"; then
      printf 'Candidate runner changed before use.\n' >&2; exit 1
    fi
    CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_NEXT"
  fi
  check_candidate_protocol
  check_live_protocol
  CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
}

check_candidate_protocol
check_live_protocol
if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin" "$RUNNER_NEXT"; then
  printf 'Candidate runner changed during validation; reconnect.
' >&2; exit 1
fi
publish_selected_runner() {
  [ "$(readlink "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$OWNER" ] || {
    printf 'Replacement lock ownership changed; runner was preserved.\n' >&2; exit 1;
  }
  check_retained_runner
if [ -f "$RUNNER_FILE" ] && cmp -s "$RUNNER_NEXT" "$RUNNER_FILE"; then
  rm -f "$RUNNER_NEXT"
else
  mv "$RUNNER_NEXT" "$RUNNER_FILE"
  RUNNER_CHANGED=1
fi
  sync_runner_alias || :
  RUNNER_PUBLISHED=1
}
pending_attachment_safe() {
  [ "$DRAIN_UNCERTAIN" = 0 ] || return 1
  # A replacement needs the mutex; lock-only contention can reuse a proven live server.
  { [ "$LOCK_HELD" = 1 ] && [ "$(readlink "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$OWNER" ]; } ||
    { [ "$reason" = contended ] && [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 0 ]; }
}
emit_pending_only() {
  printf '{"status":"pending","pending":{%s}}
' "$pending_fields"
  exit 0
}
emit_pending() {
  reason="$1"; pending_detail="${2:-}"
  [ -n "$pending_detail" ] || pending_detail="$LOCK_DETAIL"
  pending_fields="$(printf '"reason":"%s","replacement":"%s","requestedVersion":"%s","liveVersion":"%s"' "$reason" "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" "$REQUESTED_VERSION" "$LIVE_VERSION")"
  case "$pending_detail" in
    recovery-stale) pending_fields="$pending_fields,"'"detail":"recovery-stale"' ;;
    drain-unavailable) pending_fields="$pending_fields,"'"refreshCause":"drain_unavailable"' ;;
  esac
  # Reuse is independently proven using the retained runner, never the incompatible candidate.
  pending_attachment_safe || emit_pending_only
  # A server that did not answer its activity probe may not answer the app either; its HTTP
  # root alone does not prove it ready. Only a server without drain support was never asked.
  [ "$reason" != unknown ] || [ "$pending_detail" = drain-unavailable ] || emit_pending_only
  if [ "$reason" = contended ] && [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 0 ] && [ ! -f "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" ]; then
    capture_running_runner || emit_pending_only
  fi

  if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ -f "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" ] &&
     [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" = "$EXPECTED_LIVE_RUNNER_SHA256" ] &&
     [ "$("$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" --version 2>/dev/null || true)" = "goat v$LIVE_VERSION" ]; then
    retained_own="$("$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" __ssh-helper protocol --shell 2>/dev/null || true)"
    set -f; set -- $retained_own
    if valid_own_tokens "$@" && compatible_fields "$1" "$2" "$3" && [ "$1" = "$LIVE_VERSION" ] &&
       "$RETAINED_SNAPSHOT_FILE" __ssh-helper wait-ready "$LIVE_PORT" "2000" "1000" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
      pending_pid="$LIVE_PID"; pending_port="$LIVE_PORT"; pending_version="$LIVE_VERSION"
      check_retained_runner
      check_live_protocol
      pending_attachment_safe || emit_pending_only
      if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_PID" = "$pending_pid" ] && [ "$LIVE_PORT" = "$pending_port" ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$pending_version" ] &&
         { [ "$pending_detail" != drain-unavailable ] || { [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && verify_owned_identity "$LIVE_PID" "$LIVE_PORT"; }; }; then
        pending_kind=external; [ "$LIVE_OWNED" != 1 ] || pending_kind=managed
        # Lock contention does not imply a replacement; compatible attach-only servers stay ready.
        pending_suffix=
        if [ "$reason" != contended ] || [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" != 0 ]; then
          pending_suffix="$(printf ',"pending":{%s}' "$pending_fields")"
        fi
        printf '{"status":"ready","remotePort":%s,"serverKind":"%s","selectedVersion":"%s"%s}
' "$LIVE_PORT" "$pending_kind" "$LIVE_VERSION" "$pending_suffix"
        exit 0
      fi
    fi
  fi
  emit_pending_only
}
if [ "$OWNING_LAUNCH" = 1 ]; then
  acquire_replacement_lock || { wait_for_replacement_lock && acquire_replacement_lock || emit_pending contended; }
  # Classification and ordering must be fresh under the host-wide mutex.
  CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
  check_live_protocol
  RECONCILING_DRAIN=0
  if [ "$DRAIN_UNCERTAIN" = 1 ]; then
    [ "$ALLOW_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_OWNED" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_DRAIN" = 1 ] && [ -n "$LIVE_INSTANCE_ID" ] || emit_pending unknown
    # Retry the authenticated request: the server joins an active drain, confirms its
    # cancellation, or exits for the supervisor. HTTP readiness alone proves none of these.
    RECONCILING_DRAIN=1; NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$SELECTED_VERSION" ] &&
     [ "$LIVE_VERSION" = "$REQUESTED_VERSION" ] && [ -n "$REFRESH_LIVE_VERSION" ] &&
     [ "$REFRESH_LIVE_VERSION" != "$LIVE_VERSION" ]; then
    # Another owner completed this exact refresh while we waited; the old runner pin is obsolete.
    EXPECTED_LIVE_RUNNER_SHA256="$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" || ownership_unverified
  fi
  if [ "$LIVE_COMPATIBLE" = 1 ] && [ "$comparison" = newer ] && [ "$LIVE_VERSION" != "$SELECTED_VERSION" ]; then
    # Another client may have completed a newer installation since preparation.
    # Pin its independently verified retained runner rather than publish our older candidate.
    selected_dir="$HOME/.goat/runtime/goat/versions/$LIVE_VERSION"
    [ -x "$selected_dir/goat" ] && [ "$(cat "$selected_dir/.install-complete" 2>/dev/null)" = "$LIVE_VERSION" ] || ownership_unverified
    fresh_sha="$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" || ownership_unverified
    cp "$RUNNER_FILE" "$RUNNER_NEXT"
    [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_NEXT")" = "$fresh_sha" ] && [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" = "$fresh_sha" ] || ownership_unverified
    [ "$("$RUNNER_NEXT" --version 2>/dev/null || true)" = "goat v$LIVE_VERSION" ] || ownership_unverified
    pin_runner "$RUNNER_NEXT"
    SELECTED_VERSION="$LIVE_VERSION"; REQUIRE_INSTALLED=1
    EXPECTED_LIVE_RUNNER_SHA256="$fresh_sha"
    [ "$PRESERVE_SELECTED_RUNNER" = 0 ] || EXPECTED_RETAINED_SHA256="$fresh_sha"
  fi
  check_candidate_protocol
  check_retained_runner
  # Nothing since the check under the lock re-pins or changes its inputs when it found no server,
  # and the launch asks again before it acts on the answer.
  [ "$LIVE_STATUS" = none ] || check_live_protocol
  [ "$RECONCILING_DRAIN" != 1 ] || NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE=1

  [ "$DEFER_NO_DRAIN" != 1 ] || emit_pending unknown drain-unavailable
  if [ "$NEEDS_OWNED_UPGRADE" = 1 ] && [ "$RECONCILING_DRAIN" != 1 ] && [ "$REPLACEMENT_REASON" != incompatible ] && [ "$DRAIN_FORCE" != 1 ]; then
    # An optional refresh waits for idle; launch probes again last, then the server drains.
    activity="$(read_refresh_activity)"
    [ "$activity" = idle ] || emit_pending "$activity"
  fi
else
  # Pairing/MCP reuse is read-only; only initial shared setup may publish.
  if [ -f "$RUNNER_FILE" ] && [ "$LIVE_STATUS" != none ]; then
    if ! cmp -s "$RUNNER_NEXT" "$RUNNER_FILE"; then
      secondary_sha="$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" || exit 1
      cp "$RUNNER_FILE" "$RUNNER_NEXT"
      [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_NEXT")" = "$secondary_sha" ] && [ "$(runner_sha256 "$RUNNER_FILE")" = "$secondary_sha" ] || exit 1
      pin_runner "$RUNNER_NEXT"
      CHECK_RUNNER="$RUNNER_CANDIDATE_FILE.pin"
      check_candidate_protocol
      check_live_protocol
    fi
    RUNNER_PUBLISHED=1
  else
    acquire_replacement_lock || { printf 'Another client is replacing the remote runtime.
' >&2; exit 1; }
    check_live_protocol
    publish_selected_runner
  fi
fi


PAIRING_BASE_DIR="$DEFAULT_SERVER_HOME"
recheck_selected_before_use
"$RUNNER_FILE" auth pairing create --base-dir "$PAIRING_BASE_DIR" --json
